item.title: Natalie Wood's Wardrobe and Makeup Evolution: Studio Tests from the 1950s and 1960s
item.description: This article explores Natalie Wood's iconic wardrobe and makeup transformations during the 1950s and 1960s, highlighting her evolution from a child star to a mature Hollywood leading lady. In Hollywood's studio system, wardrobe and makeup tests were essential technical tools that addressed complex lighting and Technicolor palette requirements. During the mid-to-late 1950s, Wood underwent extensive tests to shed her childhood image from films like *Miracle on 34th Street*. These sessions balanced youthful innocence with emerging mature glamor, featuring natural skin tones, defined dark eyebrows, and classic red lips. She often posed near studio equipment like name placards and wooden ladders to calibrate Technicolor lighting. By the 1960s, her role shifted to managing high-fashion costume wardrobes designed by legendary creators. item.title: Mavis Tire Acquires Pep Boys to Expand Automotive Services
item.description: Mavis Tire, a leading automotive service provider, has announced plans to acquire Pep Boys, a major player in the automotive industry, to expand its market presence. The merger aims to combine Mavis Tire's extensive network of service centers with Pep Boys' established brand and customer base, creating a more comprehensive offering for consumers. The deal is expected to enhance efficiency, reduce costs, and provide better service options for customers. Financial details of the acquisition were not disclosed, but industry analysts predict the combined entity could generate significant revenue. The move reflects growing trends in the automotive sector toward consolidation to achieve economies of scale. item.title: Analyst Warns of Dire Consequences if Trump Escalates Iran Conflict
item.description: A New Republic analyst warns that President Donald Trump's potential actions in Iran could lead to catastrophic global consequences. The piece outlines four alarming scenarios, including the possibility of Trump bombing civilian infrastructure like power stations, targeting Kharg Island (which handles 90% of Iran's oil exports), launching a ground invasion, or resorting to tactical nuclear weapons if impatient for quick results. The author criticizes Trump's lack of foresight, decision-making flaws, and tendency to prioritize immediate political gains over long-term stability. The article highlights concerns about destabilizing the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil trade, and the risk of nuclear escalation due to Trump's impulsive behavior. The analyst concludes that Trump's approach to war lacks moral and strategic considerations, posing a severe threat to international security.

item.title: Amateur Astronomer Discovers 390-Million-Year-Old Meteor Crater in Quebec
item.description: In 2024, amateur astronomer Joël Lapointe stumbled upon a suspicious pit while using Google Maps to plan a camping trip in Quebec's Côte-Nord region. Researchers later confirmed it as a previously unidentified meteor crater dating back 390 million years, with a diameter of 25 kilometers. Led by planetary geologist Gordon Osinski, a team conducted a challenging field expedition to the site, overcoming rugged terrain and logistical hurdles like landing 50 meters offshore. They discovered impact melt rock formed by extreme temperatures and pressures from the meteor strike, as well as shatter cones—unique geological features found only in impact craters or nuclear test sites. The crater's age, while not exceptionally rare in geological terms, highlights Earth's ongoing surprises. Lapointe, who initially thought it might be a natural formation, expressed pride in his discovery, which was validated by experts and named Uhackatik in consultation with the Innu Council of Ekuanitshit. item.title: Froth & Fury Fest 2027 Unveils Stacked Lineup and New Initiatives for Emerging Artists
item.description: Adelaide’s Froth & Fury Festival is set to become one of Australia’s premier heavy music events in 2027, with its first lineup announcement showcasing a mix of international heavyweights and local favorites. Returning to the Adelaide Showground on January 30th, the festival has secured acts like Clutch, Alpha Wolf, Paleface Swiss, Propagandhi, Igorrr, Carpenter Brut, and Corrosion Of Conformity, alongside death metal legends Death To All and thrash icons Dark Angel. The lineup also features Australian punk veterans 28 Days and Colorado hardcore group Fox Lake. Notably, the festival is expanding its commitment to nurturing local talent through initiatives like New Breed (a competition for young musicians aged 10-18) and Path To Fury (a battle-of-the-bands contest for South Australian bands). Beyond music, attendees can enjoy tattoo artists, food trucks, and market stalls. With two more lineup drops planned, Froth & Fury 2027 promises to be a major event for heavy music fans in Australia

item.title: Nitrogen Bubbles in Titan's Methane Seas May Explain 'Magic Islands' Observed by Cassini
item.description: The article discusses the mysterious 'magic islands' observed by NASA's Cassini spacecraft in Titan's methane seas, which appeared, disappeared, and reappeared over time. Scientists propose that these phenomena could be caused by nitrogen bubbles rising through the liquid as the alien lakes warm or mix. Laboratory experiments support this theory, showing that nitrogen can dissolve in cold methane and release as bubbles when conditions change. The study highlights the dynamic nature of Titan's environment, where cryogenic processes create transient features. While the Cassini mission ended in 2017, future missions like NASA's Dragonfly rotorcraft may provide further insights. The research underscores the importance of understanding extraterrestrial chemistry and the potential for similar processes on other icy moons. The findings also emphasize the role of temperature and pressure in shaping planetary surfaces, offering a glimpse into the complex geology of Saturn's moon.

item.title: South Carolina Senator Darline Graham Announces Full Senate Bid Focusing on Domestic Issues
item.description: Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., the sister of late Sen. Lindsey Graham, has announced her candidacy for a full six-year Senate term following her brother's sudden death on July 11. In an exclusive interview with 'Hannity,' Graham emphasized her commitment to continuing her brother's legacy by prioritizing domestic issues over foreign policy. She highlighted concerns such as the cost of groceries, gas prices, healthcare, and insurance as central to her platform. Graham, South Carolina's first female U.S. Senator, expressed an 'inner peace' about succeeding her brother, noting his deep dedication to the state's residents. She also revealed her focus on practical, everyday challenges faced by South Carolinians, contrasting her approach with her brother's emphasis on national security and international affairs. Graham's decision to run for a full term comes after being appointed to complete her brother's remaining Senate term until January 2027. Her remarks underscore the political significan

item.title: Study Reveals Higher Dementia Risk in Spouses Beyond Shared Lifestyle Factors
item.description: A large-scale study from Taiwan involving nearly one million married adults found that spouses of individuals diagnosed with dementia have a significantly increased risk of developing the condition themselves. While previous smaller studies hinted at this correlation, this research is notable for its scale and depth, analyzing health records from Taiwan’s national insurance program between 1998 and 2022. The study accounted for factors like age, income, and pre-existing health conditions, revealing that women with spouses diagnosed with dementia had a 74% higher relative risk, while men faced a 69% increase. Absolute risk figures showed around 6.5% of women and 9.2% of men developed dementia within five years compared to lower rates in the control group. Researchers emphasize that this is not evidence of direct transmission but rather shared health profiles shaped by decades of similar lifestyles, environments, and behaviors. item.title: Trump Attends World Cup Final as Spain Wins Tournament, Celebrates Team's Success
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump attended the 2026 FIFA World Cup final in East Rutherford, New Jersey, where Spain defeated Argentina to claim the championship title. The event, held on July 19, 2026, drew global attention as Trump, known for his controversial political career, publicly celebrated Spain's victory. During the ceremony, Trump presented the trophy to Spain's team, including star player Ferran Torres, while FIFA President Gianni Infantino and other dignitaries were present. The U.S. presidential helicopter, Marine One, flew over the stadium prior to the match, symbolizing Trump's symbolic connection to the event. While the World Cup is a global football (soccer) tournament, Trump's attendance and public endorsement of Spain's win sparked debate about the political implications of such events. The final match highlighted Spain's tactical prowess and resilience, with Torres scoring the decisive goal in the 89th minute. Trump's presence at the ceremony, despite his political stan

item.title: Sen. Darline Graham to Run for Full Senate Term After Brother's Death
item.description: Sen. Darline Graham (R-South Carolina) has announced her intention to seek a full six-year Senate term following the death of her brother, Lindsey Graham, who passed away on July 11, 2026. South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster (R) appointed Graham last week to temporarily fill the Senate seat left vacant by her brother's death. The decision comes after President Donald Trump encouraged her to run, emphasizing the importance of her candidacy. Graham's appointment was made under the provisions of South Carolina's state law, which allows for temporary succession in such cases. The article highlights the political significance of her campaign, as she aims to continue her brother's legacy in the Senate. Her candidacy also underscores the broader implications of political succession and the role of family ties in American politics. item.title: Colorado River's Climate and Water Management Crisis
item.description: The article explores the escalating climate crisis affecting the Colorado River, highlighting how the diversion of the river for human use contributes to greenhouse gas emissions, which in turn exacerbate drought conditions in the Southwest. This creates a feedback loop where water scarcity forces policymakers to accelerate diversion efforts, further worsening the environmental impact. The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, responsible for managing the river, faces mounting pressure as negotiations and legal battles over water rights intensify. The piece argues that the agency should prioritize scientific analysis over high-stakes political decisions to address the crisis effectively. The situation underscores the interconnectedness of climate change, water management, and regional policy, with the Southwest's water security hanging in the balance. Experts warn that without sustainable solutions, the region risks irreversible ecological damage and social unrest. The article calls for a reeval

item.title: CNN Debate Over Trump Border Czar's Controversial Comments on ICE Practices
item.description: A heated exchange unfolded during a CNN segment as host Fredericka Whitfield discussed remarks by Tom Homan, President Donald Trump's border czar, who claimed that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents involved in the Minneapolis protests did not make mistakes. Christine Quinn, executive chair of the New York State Democratic Party, criticized Homan's comments as emblematic of the Trump administration's attempts to hold Democrats to strict standards while dismissing internal criticism. The discussion escalated when Stephen Moore accused Democrats of failing to reform ICE during Joe Biden's presidency, prompting Keith Boykin to counter that Trump had sabotaged bipartisan efforts. GOP pundit Scott Jennings linked Homan's remarks to an arrest involving a military veteran with anti-ICE memorabilia, suggesting a connection to Trump's policies. The debate highlighted deepening divisions over ICE's role and the politicization of law enforcement practices.

item.title: Fark.com Struggles with Ad Revenue and Survival Concerns
item.description: Fark.com, a long-standing community-driven website known for its eclectic mix of user-submitted links, absurd headlines, and internet humor, is facing significant challenges in maintaining ad revenue. The site's founder has publicly expressed concerns about its financial viability, warning that without adequate support, the platform may not survive. User comments highlight the site's decline from a quirky online hub to a polarizing space marked by political activism and contentious debates. While some users lament its transformation into an echo chamber for ideological discourse, others acknowledge its role in fostering internet culture. The article underscores broader issues about the sustainability of niche platforms in an increasingly competitive digital landscape, where monetization pressures often clash with community-driven values. Despite its struggles, Fark remains a cultural touchstone, reflecting both the vibrancy and fragility of online communities.

item.title: Army Veteran Accused of Incendiary Attack on NYC Federal Building with Anti-ICE Materials
item.description: An Army veteran, Andrew Arrabaca, 43, was arrested after allegedly setting fire to the Jacob K. Javits Federal Office Building in Lower Manhattan with gasoline and a firework canister. Authorities reported he also carried anti-ICE materials, including a sign reading 'ICE off our streets,' along with weapons like axes, hammers, and knives. The attack occurred on July 20, 2026, amid heightened tensions over immigration policies, following recent ICE-related fatalities in Maine and Texas. Arrabaca injured one civilian and two federal employees before being detained by police. FBI officials described him as an 'anti-American, anti-government extremist,' citing his actions and post-arrest statements. The incident occurred near 26 Federal Plaza, a focal point for immigration enforcement and protests, where migrants have previously been arrested during court hearings. Law enforcement is investigating potential terrorism ties, while the NYPD bomb squad examined the scene. Arrabaca’s vehicle wa

item.title: Trump's Qatari jet security concerns emerge after conflicting statements and legal actions
item.description: Jen Psaki, a journalist for MS NOW, highlighted President Donald Trump's inconsistent statements regarding the security of his Qatari-gifted Air Force One. Initially, Trump denied any safety concerns about the plane, even when reporters raised questions about its missile defense capabilities. However, Psaki revealed that Trump later admitted the plane was being mothballed for upgrades, aligning with reports from the New York Times. The administration has faced criticism for its handling of the situation, including attempts to subpoena journalists who uncovered the vulnerabilities of the aircraft. Federal agents reportedly served subpoenas to Times reporters and sought the phone records of their family members. Psaki criticized the administration's denial of the security issues and its efforts to silence the journalists. The incident underscores ongoing tensions between the Trump administration and media scrutiny, particularly regarding national security and transparency.

item.title: Tropical Storm Bertha Threatens Gulf Coast with Flooding and Strong Winds
item.description: Tropical Storm Bertha has formed in the northeastern Gulf of Mexico and is expected to impact portions of the Gulf Coast from Florida to Louisiana, potentially reaching as far west as Texas. The storm brings heavy rainfall, coastal flooding, and tropical storm-force winds. Satellite imagery shows bands of heavy rain already affecting the Florida Panhandle. With winds at 40 mph, Bertha remains an unorganized system due to dry air and its large size, despite near-record warm Gulf waters fueling its development. A tropical storm watch is in effect for areas from the Ochlockonee River in Florida to the Jefferson-Plaquemines Parish border in Louisiana, with potential conditions within 24-48 hours. Additional watches may extend westward along the Texas coast. While Bertha is unlikely to strengthen significantly due to land interaction and increasing wind shear, it could reach the Upper Texas Coast as a tropical depression by late week. Impacts include 2-4 inches of rain with localized floodi

item.title: AUKUS Inquiry in Adelaide Sparks Debate Over Security and Environmental Concerns
item.description: The article details the ongoing AUKUS inquiry in Adelaide, focusing on the potential environmental and security implications of the alliance's initiatives. Experts and stakeholders are scrutinizing the project's impact on local ecosystems and global security dynamics. The inquiry, led by Garrett, emphasizes the need for transparency and sustainable practices. Key concerns include the balance between technological advancement and ecological preservation, as well as the geopolitical ramifications of the alliance. The article highlights calls for public engagement and rigorous oversight to ensure the project aligns with both national interests and environmental standards. It underscores the complexity of navigating modern security challenges while addressing ecological responsibilities, reflecting broader debates about the role of international alliances in shaping global priorities.

item.title: Border Czar Tom Homan defends ICE actions amid controversy over fatal incidents
item.description: Tom Homan, President Donald Trump's border czar, sparked controversy during a press briefing at the White House by making contentious claims about ICE-related fatalities. Discussing the deaths of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas and Joán Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Maine, Homan asserted that many incidents attributed to ICE were not mistakes but rather cases where victims failed to comply with law enforcement protocols. He stated, 'These people failed to comply with law enforcement... all they had to do is comply. If they did, they'd be alive today.' His remarks drew sharp criticism from journalists and analysts, who questioned the official narrative surrounding ICE operations. Homan also expressed frustration over security measures, complaining that he cannot purchase milk without a personal security detail, calling it 'pathetic and disgusting.' item.title: New Orleans Police Department Releases Draft Policy Allowing Weaponized Drones, Despite Current Ban
item.description: A draft New Orleans Police Department (NOPD) drone manual, briefly published online, would have allowed police drones to carry weapons with written approval from the superintendent, according to 404 Media. NOPD clarified the document was an early draft, and their current policy (PDF) explicitly bans drones from carrying weapons or hazardous materials. The current version of the policy states, 'The sUAS shall not be equipped with weapons or hazardous materials of any kind,' referring to small Unmanned Aerial Systems. NOPD emphasized that the published manual was a draft version, and the current policy is the official version. The incident highlights tensions between internal police planning and public policy, as New Orleans has a history of controversial policing tactics. Critics argue that the draft's existence suggests ongoing consideration of weaponized drones, despite official prohibitions. The article also notes broader implications for law enforcement's use of drones, with debates

item.title: Melatonin Offers Modest Relief for Chronic Muscle and Joint Pain
item.description: A study suggests melatonin may provide mild relief for chronic muscle and joint pain, though its effects are limited. Researchers analyzed 23 clinical trials involving over 2,000 participants, finding that melatonin reduced pain scores by about nine points on a 100-point scale. However, the benefits are modest compared to anti-inflammatory drugs, and the drug's effectiveness may depend on pre-existing sleep issues or health conditions. The study also found limited impact on post-surgical pain, with only a 2.5-point improvement. While melatonin is generally safe for short-term use, side effects like dizziness and nausea may occur. Regulatory differences exist globally, with the U.S. classifying it as a supplement and the UK requiring a prescription. The findings indicate melatonin could complement existing treatments like physiotherapy and anti-inflammatory medications but should not replace them. Further research is needed to determine optimal dosages and target populations.

item.title: Vanilla Reigns as America's Most Popular Ice Cream Flavor in 2025
item.description: A comprehensive analysis of U.S. ice cream preferences reveals that vanilla remains the undisputed leader, dominating sales across all regions. According to data from Instacart and Google search trends, vanilla accounts for approximately 24% of orders, surpassing brands like Ben & Jerry's and Breyers. The article highlights how regional flavors also thrive, with Tillamook leading in the West, Blue Bell in the South, and Blue Bunny in the Plains. While Halo Top was the most-searched brand in 2026, traditional favorites like chocolate and cookie dough continue to anchor freezer shelves. The piece emphasizes that America's ice cream culture is a blend of comfort-driven classics and localized specialties, with newer 'better-for-you' options gradually gaining traction. Regional variations include Rocky Road in the West, coffee in New England, and butter pecan in the South. Despite growing interest in premium and specialty brands, vanilla's versatility as a neutral base ensures its enduring

item.title: QAnon Supporters Plan Sanctuary for Trafficked Children
item.description: A group of QAnon adherents has taken control of a decommissioned women's prison in California, aiming to transform it into a 'sanctuary' for children allegedly trafficked by global elites. The project, backed by $1.6 million in donations, is organized by far-right pastor David Bryan and involves fundraising through the 'Rev17 2.0' conference, which features prominent conspiracy theorists like Lara Logan and Ann Vandersteel. The initiative draws parallels to extremist ideologies, with critics comparing QAnon's conspiratorial narratives to Nazism due to their shared reliance on fabricated conspiracies about elite control over society. The article highlights how the group plans to use the prison as a safe space for rescued children while continuing to solicit funds through events tied to apocalyptic themes from the Book of Revelation. item.title: China's Village Super League: A Local Soccer Phenomenon Boosting Economy and Community Spirit
item.description: The article details China's 'Village Super League,' an amateur soccer tournament gaining nationwide popularity as a vibrant alternative to the World Cup. Held in rural areas like Fuping county, Hebei province, the league features teams composed of everyday workers, teachers, and students competing for national championships. Local governments have actively supported the initiative to stimulate economic growth and tourism, with events attracting thousands of spectators and boosting consumer spending. The tournament contrasts sharply with China's professional leagues plagued by corruption and mismanagement, offering a grassroots celebration of soccer that fosters community pride. While the Chinese men’s team hasn’t qualified for the World Cup since 2002, the Village Super League provides a platform for local passion, uniting residents through sports and cultural events that highlight regional development and collective spirit.

item.title: Colossal Biosciences Expands with $20B–$30B Valuation Amid De-Extinction and Tech Innovations
item.description: Colossal Biosciences, a de-extinction startup known for its efforts to resurrect extinct species like the dire wolf, is reportedly in discussions to raise new capital at a valuation between $20 billion and $30 billion. This follows its previous $10.2 billion valuation and marks significant growth over 16 months. The company has already begun generating revenue through contracts with the U.S. government and the UAE, which invested $60 million in 2025. Colossal has spun off three startups, including Breaking (plastic breakdown), Form Bio (computational biology), and Astromech (AI-driven predictive modeling). CEO Ben Lamm highlighted plans to commercialize artificial animal womb technology for human fertility applications, expected by 2027. The fundraising comes amid a boom in deep-tech sectors like longevity tech and alternative energy. item.title: Senator Mark Kelly Criticizes Trump's Cognitive Abilities Amid Political Tensions
item.description: Senator Mark Kelly, a retired Navy captain and astronaut, faced political scrutiny after making a pointed remark about President Donald Trump's cognitive abilities during an interview with The Atlantic. Kelly, who has been speculated as a potential 2028 presidential candidate, was asked about America's readiness for a 'disabled first lady' following his wife Gabby Giffords' 2011 shooting incident. Kelly responded by criticizing Trump's mental state, stating, 'In my opinion, we have a pretty disabled president right now.' This comment comes amid ongoing tensions between Kelly and Trump, fueled by Kelly's participation in a video with other military veteran Democrats urging servicemembers to refuse illegal orders. Trump's Secretary of Defense, Pete Hegseth, threatened to court-martial Kelly but ultimately sought to demote his rank, sparking months of legal battles. item.title: Military Politicization and the Future of Defense Reform
item.description: The article discusses the growing concerns over the politicization of the U.S. military, particularly highlighting the appointment of Pete Hegseth as a key figure in shaping defense policy. Author Michael Ramirez critiques how political agendas are increasingly influencing military operations, raising alarms about the potential erosion of institutional integrity. The piece examines historical precedents of military politicization, such as the Vietnam War era, and compares them to contemporary challenges like the Afghanistan withdrawal. Ramirez argues that while civilian oversight is essential, excessive political interference risks compromising operational effectiveness and national security. The article also touches on the role of media in amplifying partisan narratives around military decisions, suggesting that public discourse often lacks nuance. item.title: Six recalled products pose safety risks
item.description: The article highlights six consumer products that have been recalled due to safety hazards. These items, ranging from kitchen appliances to personal care products, pose potential risks to users. Manufacturers issued recalls after identifying defects that could lead to injuries or property damage. Consumers are advised to check for recall notices from the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) or visit the companies' websites for detailed information. The article emphasizes the importance of staying informed about product recalls to protect household safety. It also mentions that some recalls are voluntary, while others are mandated by regulatory agencies. Consumers should stop using recalled items immediately and follow instructions for returning or disposing of them. The piece serves as a reminder to regularly check for recall alerts and prioritize product safety in daily life.

item.title: Major Sporting Events' Emissions Stem from Spectator Travel, Study Finds
item.description: A new study by the University of Cambridge reveals that spectator travel accounts for 82% of greenhouse gas emissions from large-scale events like the FIFA World Cup. Analyzing the 2026 World Cup and Coldplay’s 2024 European tour, researchers found that fan travel generated 3.07 million metric tons of CO2 equivalent, surpassing Iceland’s annual emissions. The study highlights that expanding the World Cup to 48 teams increased emissions by 590,000 metric tons, with international travel being the primary contributor. Coldplay’s tour reduced emissions by 48% through fan behavioral changes like low-carbon travel options and discounts. The research proposes a two-stage framework for event organizers to balance economic benefits with climate costs, suggesting higher-tier tickets should bear greater carbon levies. The findings emphasize the need for shared responsibility between organizers and fans to mitigate emissions from mega-events, which are increasingly challenged by climate change imp

item.title: A Glimpse into Early 20th-Century Beverage Advertising Art
item.description: This article showcases a collection of beautifully illustrated vintage beverage advertisements from the early 1900s, highlighting their artistic creativity and sophisticated marketing techniques. The ads feature sodas, coffees, teas, wines, and tonics with refined typography, charming illustrations, and persuasive messaging that reflect the optimism and consumer culture of the Edwardian and Art Deco eras. Examples include Absinthe Blanqui from Nice (circa 1900), Bitter Campari (1900), and Coca-Cola's first advertisement (1904). These pieces not only promoted products but also captured the aesthetic trends and societal values of the time, serving as both commercial tools and artistic expressions. The collection offers insight into how brands engaged with audiences through visual storytelling, blending commerce with cultural narratives.

item.title: Liberals' Shift in Attitude Toward Trump Amidst War Policies
item.description: The article discusses how the liberal establishment has become significantly less critical of Donald Trump during his second term compared to his first. This shift is attributed to Trump's actions, such as bombing Iran, which have reassured elites that he will continue to support U.S. military interventions and maintain imperial policies. The author argues that liberals previously criticized Trump for perceived isolationist tendencies, but now they view him as a reliable steward of the empire. The piece highlights how Trump's domestic policies are seen as more authoritarian and his corruption evident, yet liberals have grown complacent with his governance. It critiques the media's role in amplifying such narratives and questions the ethical implications of supporting leaders who perpetuate conflict. The summary emphasizes the political dynamics at play and the potential consequences of prioritizing imperial interests over public welfare.

item.title: Dollar Tree Closes 75 Stores Amid Expansion Plans
item.description: Dollar Tree, a popular discount retailer, announced plans to close approximately 75 underperforming stores nationwide during fiscal 2026 while simultaneously expanding its physical presence by opening around 400 new locations. The strategy reflects a broader shift toward targeting higher-income demographics in more affluent areas, aiming to boost average spending per customer. CEO Mike Creedon emphasized the company's focus on improving store conditions, expanding product offerings, and strengthening customer relationships as part of its long-term growth plan. This move comes amid rising consumer concerns about financial stability due to surging rent and food costs, according to recent Federal Reserve data. The retailer has already opened 113 stores in the first quarter of 2026, bringing its total U.S. and Canadian footprint to 9,382 locations. Dollar Tree also converted or added approximately 630 stores to its multi-price format, allowing about 5,900 locations to sell products at vari

item.title: Moonshot AI Pauses New Subscriptions for Popular Kimi K3 Model Due to High Demand
item.description: Moonshot AI, a Beijing-based company, has temporarily paused new subscriptions for its Kimi K3 AI model after experiencing overwhelming demand that exceeded its current capacity. The open-source model, with 2.8 trillion parameters, has outperformed U.S. rivals like Anthropic's Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 in coding tests, sparking significant interest. However, the surge in demand has strained Moonshot's compute infrastructure, leading to a temporary halt on new subscriptions. The company prioritizes existing subscribers and plans to reopen subscriptions in batches as capacity expands. Analysts note that Moonshot likely underestimated the model's popularity, with K3's high computational demands making resource allocation challenging and expensive. While the model's success highlights advancements in AI, concerns remain about scalability and the sustainability of such rapid growth. item.title: Spain's World Cup Photo Excludes Trump, Sparking Global Reaction
item.description: Following Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in the FIFA World Cup final on July 19, 2026, President Donald Trump attempted to photobomb the trophy presentation ceremony. However, the Spanish Football Federation's official X post featured players and coach Luis de la Fuente celebrating without any sign of Trump, prompting widespread speculation that he was digitally removed from the image. Social media users worldwide mocked the suspected edit, with Democratic influencer Harry Sisson commenting, 'LOL SPAIN EDITED TRUMP OUT OF THE PHOTO,' and sportswriter Amos Murphy questioning if the photo was altered. The incident highlights tensions between Trump and international football authorities, as well as his controversial presence at major events. While some critics argued the exclusion was a political move, others suggested it reflected broader frustrations with Trump's behavior during the ceremony.

item.title: Domino's Expands into Burgers Amid Pizza Industry Growth
item.description: Domino's, the iconic pizza delivery chain, is making a strategic move into the burger market as it seeks to capitalize on the growing demand for convenience foods. The company, known for its rapid delivery and digital ordering systems, has announced plans to launch a line of burgers in select markets. This expansion comes as the pizza industry faces increasing competition from other fast-food chains and the rise of plant-based alternatives. Analysts suggest that Domino's decision to enter the burger segment is driven by its desire to diversify its revenue streams and attract a broader customer base. The move also reflects a broader trend in the food industry where companies are blending traditional offerings with modern conveniences. While some critics argue that Domino's may struggle to compete with established burger brands, others believe its strong brand recognition and delivery infrastructure could give it an edge. The company's stock has seen a slight uptick following the announc

item.title: Trump Shares Photo of JD Vance and Usha Vance's Newborn Son
item.description: President Donald Trump posted an image of Vice President JD Vance and second lady Usha Vance's newborn son, Alec Neel Vance, on Truth Social before the couple officially announced the birth. The Vances, who are the first sitting vice president and spouse to have a child since the 1870s, shared a statement confirming the birth of their fourth child, describing the baby as healthy and the family as joyful. Trump praised the newborn as the 'perfect baby boy' in his post, showcasing a photo of Vivek holding the new sibling with Mirabel watching. The Vances thanked medical staff at Walter Reed Medical Center and the White House Medical Unit for their care. JD Vance mentioned he would likely be at the White House more frequently due to his duties, while Usha Vance would take a break from public appearances. The couple's announcement highlights the rare occurrence of a vice president's child being born while in office, emphasizing the blend of personal and political moments in their lives.

item.title: Key Health Insights for Women Navigating Aging: Menstrual Health, Weight Management, and Beyond
item.description: The article explores critical health considerations for women as they age, emphasizing functional fitness over appearance. Experts caution against normalizing severe menstrual pain or unexplained weight gain, stressing the importance of medical consultation before taking dietary supplements. The discussion highlights how hormonal fluctuations during perimenopause can impact weight, and the necessity of comprehensive blood tests to identify nutrient deficiencies. Traditional remedies like unripe mangoes and black sesame seeds are mentioned as ancient wisdom for modern health challenges. The piece underscores that aging involves physical, social, psychological, and emotional dimensions, urging women to focus on health, mobility, and self-awareness rather than superficial concerns. It also addresses topics like skincare, sexual health, and the role of hormone balance in managing symptoms, concluding that proactive health management can transform the aging journey into an empowering experi

item.title: FBI Director Kash Patel's Russia Trip Sparks Scrutiny Amid Spending Probe
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel is planning a rare trip to Russia in October, marking the first such visit by an FBI director in 13 years. The trip comes amid heightened tensions between Washington and Moscow over Ukraine and as lawmakers push for sanctions against Russia. While details of the agenda remain unclear, the visit has drawn criticism due to Patel's history of involvement in controversial Russia-related matters, including his past role in questioning investigations into Trump's alleged collusion with Russia during the 2016 election. The trip could further fuel congressional scrutiny of Patel's spending and decisions, especially as Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche faces confirmation hearings. U.S. intelligence has long warned that Moscow is behind efforts to disrupt American elections and cyberattacks on government agencies, findings supported by recently declassified documents. Patel's planned visit adds another layer of controversy to his already scrutinized tenure.

item.title: High Court Rules Receivers Can Sell Property Despite Mental Health Debt Moratorium
item.description: The High Court ruled that a mental health crisis moratorium did not prevent receivers from selling property used to secure a company loan, as the debt being enforced was owed by the company rather than the individual owner. The case involved Together Commercial Finance and Ameycroft Leisure, where a £2.4 million loan was granted in 2023. The company’s director, Stuart Slack, personally guaranteed the debt, while his son Matthew Slack provided additional security by charging his property, Farley Meadow View. After Ameycroft defaulted, receivers appointed by Together sought to sell Farley Meadow View to recover the debt. Matthew Slack claimed the sale was prohibited under a mental health crisis moratorium he entered in 2026. However, Judge Jonathan Klein clarified that the moratorium protected only personal debts, not company obligations. The property secured the company’s debt, not Slack’s personal liabilities, allowing the receivers to proceed with the sale. The court also criticized t

item.title: Young Sauropods Could Stand Upright, Study Suggests
item.description: A study published in Palaeontology reveals that certain smaller sauropod dinosaurs, such as Uberabatitan and Neuquensaurus, could stand on their hind legs with surprising ease during their juvenile stages. This ability allowed them to access higher food sources and gain a defensive advantage. Researchers used digital biomechanical models to analyze the stress resistance of these dinosaurs' bones, finding that their robust femurs could handle the physical demands of bipedal posture. However, as these dinosaurs matured, their bones became too fragile to sustain upright standing, forcing them to revert to quadrupedal movement. The study highlights how evolutionary adaptations in bone structure enabled these prehistoric giants to exploit ecological niches temporarily before their physiology limited such behaviors. This discovery challenges previous assumptions about dinosaur locomotion and underscores the complexity of biomechanical constraints in ancient species. The findings also provide

item.title: Democrats Condemn Republican Budget Policies Amid Rising National Debt Concerns
item.description: During a House Rules Committee hearing, Democratic Rep. Jim McGovern sharply criticized Republican Rep. Jodey Arrington over a budget resolution that adds $4.7 trillion to the national debt without offsets. McGovern accused Republicans of avoiding responsibility for Trump-era spending policies, noting the debt surged from $36.2 trillion to $39.5 trillion since 2017. Arrington defended the plan, claiming it was an emergency measure, while McGovern argued tax cuts for billionaires and corporate funding for Iran conflicts exemplify reckless spending. The debate highlighted deep partisan divides over fiscal priorities, with Democrats emphasizing the need to address family costs like rent and healthcare, whereas Republicans blamed previous administrations for inflation. McGovern criticized Republicans for prioritizing wealthy interests over middle-class concerns, calling their approach 'fundamental values questions.' item.title: Federal Judge Halts $110B Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger Over Antitrust Concerns
item.description: A federal judge temporarily blocked Paramount Skydance’s $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, citing antitrust concerns raised by 12 Democratic state attorneys general. The lawsuit, filed last week, argues the merger would create a media giant with excessive market power, stifling competition in Hollywood and the television news industry. The decision, issued on July 20, 2026, marks a significant setback for the deal, which was expected to reshape content production, distribution, and media consolidation. The judge’s order is a preliminary measure, pending further legal review, but it signals growing regulatory scrutiny of major corporate mergers in the entertainment sector. item.title: Viking 1's 1976 Mars Landing: A Historic First for Human Exploration
item.description: The Viking 1 mission, launched by NASA in 1976, marked a pivotal moment in space exploration as it became the first spacecraft to successfully land on Mars and transmit images of the planet's surface back to Earth. The landing on July 20, 1976, in Chryse Planitia, was a culmination of years of planning and technological innovation. The Viking 1 lander, weighing 575 kilograms, descended through Mars' thin atmosphere using a combination of parachutes and retrothrusters, avoiding a potential collision with a nearby rock. The successful landing allowed scientists to study the Martian surface, including its soil composition and potential for microbial life. The mission's scientific instruments, including a gas chromatograph-mass spectrometer (GC-MS), were designed to detect organic molecules, though no definitive signs of life were found. Noetra, a Japanese consortium led by SoftBank, Sony, NEC, and Honda, will oversee the $6.2 billion AI initiative, including a massive Vera Rubin AI factory set for 2028. The project spans three stages: a Japanese-language reasoning model by 2026, an omni-modal system by 2028, and 'Real-world Native AI' for robots by 2030. Toyota and other manufacturers are integrating Nvidia's Cosmos models into production lines and autonomous vehicles. Japan's strategy includes 10 million AI-equipped robots by 2040, backed by $65 billion in investment, as the country seeks to lead in physical AI amid global competition with the U.S. and China.

item.title: Greg Kroah-Hartman Advocates Rust for Linux's Future, Citing Bug Reduction and Developer Efficiency
item.description: Greg Kroah-Hartman, a key Linux kernel maintainer, has become a strong advocate for Rust, arguing that its ownership model and type system can significantly reduce common vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel. During his keynote at the Open Source Summit India 2026, he highlighted how Rust's features eliminate 'stupid little tiny things' that dominate kernel Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs). He noted that over 13 CVEs per day are fixed in Linux, primarily due to simple C mistakes like unchecked pointers and forgotten unlocks. Kroah-Hartman emphasized that Rust's compiler catches these errors early, making code safer and reducing the workload for maintainers. He also mentioned that new drivers for key subsystems are now only accepted in Rust, with the Android Binder IPC mechanism transitioning from C to Rust. While acknowledging Rust's learning curve, he stressed that it makes programming more efficient and enjoyable, allowing developers to focus on logic rather than debugging.

item.title: Alfred Meyer Challenges New York Times' Radiation Safety Narrative
item.description: Alfred Meyer, a prominent figure in Physicians for Social Responsibility, criticizes a New York Times article that advocates for relaxing radiation safety regulations to boost nuclear energy expansion. Meyer argues that the article lacks rigorous scientific evidence and fails to address the complexities of low-dose radiation effects. He highlights the 2006 National Academy of Sciences report supporting the Linear No-Threshold (LNT) model, which the 2021 NRC decision to retain LNT further validates. Meyer points out the Times' omission of decades of research on radiation's health impacts, including historical censorship of nuclear industry risks. He also references William Laurence's role in downplaying atomic bomb effects and Matthew Wald's transition from journalism to nuclear industry advocacy, suggesting a pattern of media bias. Meyer emphasizes the need for thorough public discourse on radiation safety, warning that the article promotes nuclear expansion without adequate scrutiny.

item.title: Health Impacts of Night Shifts and Biphasic Sleep Solutions
item.description: The article explores the health risks associated with night shifts, including increased risks of dementia, heart disease, and cancer, linked to disrupted sleep patterns and the body's circadian rhythms. It delves into the role of the glymphatic system, which clears brain waste, and how sleep deprivation impairs its function. Researchers like Dr. Moen and Dr. Foster discuss biphasic sleep—a pattern of two distinct sleep periods—as a potential solution for shift workers. Historical context is provided, noting that pre-industrial societies often slept in two blocks, a practice that may have biological roots. The piece highlights the lack of scientific consensus on biphasic sleep's benefits but emphasizes the need for guidelines to help shift workers manage sleep disruptions. It concludes with the importance of aligning with the body's natural rhythms rather than fighting them, suggesting that naps and structured sleep schedules could improve health and safety for night shift workers.

item.description: The article discusses the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission's (NRC) proposal to weaken radiation protection standards under President Trump's directive, despite scientific evidence indicating current standards underestimate health risks. The research, led by Dr. Markus Drexl, explores how the human auditory system processes low-frequency sounds and infrasound, which are below 20 Hz. The study found that while the hum is not a physical sound, it could be caused by the perception of infrasound generated by natural phenomena like ocean waves, wind, or industrial activity. The team analyzed data from individuals who reported hearing the hum and found correlations with environmental factors. item.title: Efforts to Preserve Somalia’s Radio Mogadishu Archive Amid Deterioration
item.description: A team in Somalia is working to digitize and preserve over 400,000 hours of broadcasts from Radio Mogadishu, the country's oldest public radio station. Founded in 1951 during colonial rule, the archive contains critical historical records, including news bulletins, speeches, music, and cultural content dating back to the 1950s. Despite its significance, the collection faces risks of deterioration due to age and past damage from events like an electrical fire in 2018 and conflicts in 1992. UNESCO and Somalia’s information ministry are collaborating to safeguard these materials, which hold immense cultural and historical value. The project highlights the station's role in anti-colonial movements and its efforts to promote Somali literacy. However, with the collapse of central governance in 1991, Radio Mogadishu has diminished in influence, making preservation efforts increasingly urgent to prevent gaps in Somalia’s documentary history.

item.title: Astronomers Confirm Atmosphere on Rocky Exoplanet in a Habitable Zone
item.description:
Astronomers have confirmed that the rocky exoplanet LHS 1140 b possesses an atmosphere while orbiting within the habitable zone of its host star, making it one of the most promising Earth-like worlds discovered so far. Located about 48 light-years away, the planet was first identified in 2017, but new observations collected in 2024 and 2025 provided the evidence needed to verify the presence of an atmosphere.
Researchers from the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics detected helium escaping from the planet, a finding that strongly suggests an atmosphere has existed there for at least three billion years. The team identified the helium through its spectral signature and used physical models to determine how the gas is leaking into space.

item.title: Red Blood Cell Parameters Show Potential in Differentiating Parkinsonian Syndromes
item.description: A study published in Scientific Reports explores the use of red blood cell-derived parameters, particularly red cell distribution width-coefficient of variation (RDW-CV), as a potential tool for differentiating atypical parkinsonian syndromes from Parkinson’s disease. The research analyzed 30 patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD), 29 with PSP-Richardson’s Syndrome (PSP-RS), 17 with PSP-Parkinsonism Predominant (PSP-P), and 23 healthy controls. Blood samples were evaluated to identify biomarkers that could aid in differential diagnosis. The findings revealed that elevated RDW-CV values were significantly associated with PSP-RS, showing distinct differences compared to other groups. This suggests that RDW-CV could serve as a supplementary diagnostic tool, especially given the overlapping clinical features of PSP and PD. item.description: A rare type of meteorite known as a CO chondrite was likely the object that slammed into Earth 66 million years ago and triggered the extinction of about 75 percent of all species, including every non-avian dinosaur. Researchers from the University of British Columbia (UBC), Paris, Brussels, and Vienna analyzed nickel isotopes preserved in material left behind by the Cretaceous-Paleogene impact to narrow down the meteorite's origin. The study, published in Science Advances, suggests that the asteroid's unusual chemistry indicates planet-cooling dust and debris, rather than sulfur inside the asteroid, may have caused the mass extinction. CO chondrites contain significantly less volatile elements like carbon, zinc, water, and sulfur compared to other meteorites, making it less likely that sulfur was the primary factor in the catastrophe. item.title: Prenatal Estrogen and Finger Lengths May Link to Human Brain Evolution
item.description: A study published in Early Human Development suggests that prenatal estrogen exposure may have contributed to the evolution of larger human brains. This connection was not observed in girls. The findings support the 'estrogenized ape hypothesis,' proposing that human brain expansion occurred alongside skeletal feminization. While higher estrogen exposure in males is linked to health risks like cardiovascular issues and schizophrenia, the study suggests these trade-offs may have driven evolutionary advantages. The 2D:4D ratio serves as an indirect marker of fetal hormonal exposure, offering clues about prenatal influences on human evolution. item.title: Intermittent Fasting May Aid Long-Term Weight Management
item.description: A 12-week intermittent fasting program demonstrated sustained weight loss benefits for up to a year after the intervention ended, according to a study by the University of Granada published in Clinical Nutrition. The research involved 98 participants who followed an 8-hour time-restricted eating schedule, with results showing significant weight maintenance compared to standard dieting. Key findings include: 1) Participants who fasted for 16 hours daily maintained weight loss for 12 months, while continuous calorie restriction groups saw greater weight regain. 2) The study tracked metabolic markers and body composition, revealing preserved muscle mass and improved insulin sensitivity. 3) Both 16:8 fasting and 18:6 time-restricted eating showed similar effectiveness, with no significant differences in weight loss outcomes. 4) The study challenges previous claims that intermittent fasting is less effective than traditional dieting for long-term weight management. item.title: NASA's New Horizons Probe Resumes Science Operations in the Kuiper Belt After Hibernation
item.description: NASA's New Horizons spacecraft, launched in 2006 and famously flown by Pluto in 2015, has resumed scientific operations after emerging from a planned hibernation mode. The probe, now 5.9 billion miles from Earth, awakened on June 23, 2026, after entering a dormant state on August 7, 2025. Engineers at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory confirmed the spacecraft is in excellent condition and transmitting data collected during its long sleep. The mission is now studying the Kuiper Belt, a region of icy trans-Neptunian objects, to understand planetary formation. New Horizons is analyzing the rotation, orientation, and shape of these bodies, revealing that paired, snowman-shaped objects like Arrokoth are more common than expected. This data could shed light on how planets form from dust and pebbles. item.title: Research Reveals Coffee's Health Benefits Linked to Cellular Receptor Activation
item.description: Scientists from Texas A&M University have uncovered how certain compounds in coffee may protect cells from stress, inflammation, and damage by activating the NR4A1 receptor. This receptor plays a critical role in aging, stress responses, and disease prevention. The study, published in Nutrients, found that plant-based compounds like caffeic acid are more effective than caffeine itself in interacting with NR4A1. Laboratory models showed these compounds reduce cellular damage and slow cancer cell growth, but these protective effects disappeared when the receptor was removed. While caffeine is a major component of coffee, the research suggests natural polyhydroxy and polyphenolic compounds in coffee have stronger impacts on NR4A1. The findings explain why both caffeinated and decaffeinated coffee are linked to similar health benefits. These devices, often called 'moon shoes' or 'spring-heel shoes,' were precursors to modern rebound boots like Kangoo Jumps. The text describes how these toys featured metal coil springs attached to wooden or metal platforms and were designed for kids (or adults) to bounce like kangaroos or walk on the moon. However, they were unstable and dangerous, often leading to injuries. The article also highlights their connection to the space race hype of the 1950s and contrasts them with modern fitness rebound boots developed in the 1990s by brands like Kangoo Jumps. These contemporary versions use advanced polyurethane springs for low-impact exercise, reducing joint stress by up to 80%. item.title: Study Finds Link Between Social Media Use and ADHD Symptoms in Teen Boys
item.description: A new study by researchers at the University of California at San Francisco explores the connection between addictive social media use and ADHD symptoms in adolescent boys. The research followed over 11,000 U.S. adolescents aged 12-16, tracking their social media habits and ADHD symptoms annually. Findings revealed that increases in addictive social media use were associated with rising ADHD symptoms one year later, particularly among boys aged 14-15. This correlation was not observed in reverse, suggesting social media use may exacerbate ADHD symptoms rather than being a pre-existing condition. Lead author Jason Nagata highlighted that social media platforms are designed to provide constant stimulation, encouraging task-switching and immediate gratification, which can impair attention and executive control needed for schoolwork and daily life. item.title: Avocados May Help Lower Cholesterol and Reduce Heart Disease Risk
item.description: A new study published in the Journal of Clinical Lipidology suggests that consuming avocados daily could significantly lower 'bad' cholesterol levels and reduce heart disease risk. The research, conducted over six months, involved 786 adults with abdominal obesity. Participants who added one avocado per day to their diet without changing other habits saw a 4% reduction in heart disease risk, equivalent to a 49 nanomoles per litre decrease in low-density lipoprotein (LDL) particle concentrations. Lead author Janhavi Damani noted that avocados' monounsaturated fats, fiber, and phytosterols likely contributed to the cholesterol reduction. Senior author Kristina Petersen emphasized that while this modest improvement is less impactful than overhauling the entire diet, small dietary changes like adding avocados could help people achieve sustainable health improvements over time. item.title: Evolution of Kersal, Salford: A Decades-Long Transformation Through Photography
item.description: This article presents a compelling visual journey through the transformation of Kersal, a district of Salford, Greater Manchester, over the past six decades. Dr. Shane's then-and-now photographs contrast images from the 1960s and 1970s with recent snapshots, revealing dramatic changes in architecture, urban landscapes, and daily life. The photos document the shift from traditional terraced houses and local shops to modern developments, highlighting both physical alterations and socio-economic shifts. Notable changes include the demolition of key buildings like Spencer House and Shelley House, leaving sites to become overgrown. The series also captures moments like parades, football games, and street scenes, illustrating how the neighborhood has evolved while preserving its historical essence. These images serve as a testament to urban development and the passage of time in this part of Greater Manchester.

item.description: This article explores Brian May's transformative journey during the 1970s as he evolved from a postgraduate physics student into one of rock music's most iconic guitarists. As the sonic architect of Queen, May developed a distinctive playing style centered around his custom-built 'Red Special' guitar, crafted with materials like 18th-century wood and motorcycle springs. His innovative use of multi-tracking created orchestral textures without synthesizers, as seen on Queen's groundbreaking album *A Night at the Opera*. Beyond music, May balanced his academic pursuits in interplanetary dust research with a flamboyant stage persona, including his signature Zandra Rhodes satin top. The piece highlights how his unique blend of scientific rigor and artistic creativity redefined rock guitar during the 1970s, cementing Queen's legacy as pioneers of progressive music.

item.title: Defenders Use Prompt Injections to Halt AI Hacking Agents
item.description: Researchers from Tracebit have discovered that placing prompt injections alongside sensitive data in cloud environments can effectively stop AI hacking agents. By embedding forbidden commands into decoy secrets stored on AWS, defenders trigger a shutdown mechanism in large language models (LLMs), preventing them from executing harmful actions. This technique, called 'context bombing,' forces LLMs to refuse subsequent commands, thwarting attacks that previously relied on prompt injections to exfiltrate data or gain admin access. Testing showed that context bombing reduced successful attack rates across five leading models from 57% to 5%, with the most capable agent failing entirely when confronted with these prompts. The method builds on earlier work using 'canary' resources to detect AI threats, offering a proactive defense against agentic adversaries. This marks the first known case where defenders repurpose prompt injection vulnerabilities as a countermeasure.

Poor water visibility due to depth and pollution, combined with corrosion and structural degradation, led to the aircraft's remains breaking apart within months. The pandemic further exacerbated the situation by forcing closures of the site, which remained unused for over a year. Illegal fishing activities in 2021 reportedly destroyed remaining parts of the plane, prompting authorities to obscure its location on maps. Despite initial media hype and international attention, the project ultimately failed to attract significant visitors or maintain operational viability. item.title: Antidepressant Shows Promise in Alleviating Long COVID Fatigue
item.description: A global clinical trial led by McMaster University and international collaborators found that fluvoxamine, a low-cost antidepressant, significantly reduces fatigue and improves quality of life in adults with long COVID. The randomized, placebo-controlled study involving 399 participants demonstrated that fluvoxamine outperformed both metformin and a placebo in alleviating persistent fatigue, a common and debilitating symptom of long COVID. The trial, published in the Annals of Internal Medicine, used an adaptive Bayesian design to expedite results while maintaining scientific rigor. Researchers note that while fluvoxamine shows promise for fatigue management, it is not a cure-all for long COVID, which involves multiple symptoms and biological factors. The study highlights the need for further research to identify optimal patient populations and mechanisms of action. This finding offers clinicians their first strong evidence-based treatment option for long COVID fatigue, providing hope

item.title: SpaceX Open-Sources Grok Build Tool After Privacy Concerns and Data Retention Revisions

item.title: EV Charging Infrastructure Has Improved Dramatically Over Three Years
item.description: The article details a recent 600-mile road trip using an Audi e-tron, highlighting significant improvements in EV charging infrastructure compared to three years ago. The author used ABRP app for route planning and encountered minimal issues, with chargers operating reliably and efficiently. Data from 2023 shows a substantial increase in DC fast chargers across the U.S., now exceeding twice the number available then. Reliability metrics have improved by nearly 10 points, reaching mid-90s on Paren’s index. While gaps remain, the expansion of networks like Tesla and competition among providers has enhanced overall charging experiences. The trip included stops at Rivian and Circuit Électrique stations, with only one minor hitch involving a faulty card reader. The author emphasizes that modern EV charging is nearly seamless, contrasting sharply with past frustrations. item.description: A Washington Post report detailed the violent history of David Brouillette, an ICE agent who fatally shot Colombian man Joan Sebastian Guerrero during a traffic stop in Maine.
